experiments.data_version: RES-STAGE-0.5-REAL-REF-R2; Stage 0.2 R4 four states + final_r1 P2 + Stage 0.3 R2 canonical/R3 summaries
experiments.current_conclusion: AAD-0.5-METHOD-EXPANSION executed the literature-verified method expansion and diagnosed the real-to-SUMO mismatch across initialization, structure, parameters and randomness. Phase P2: all behavioural phases are present in the trajectories (stationary 40/52 %, accelerating 32/25 %, decelerating 28/24 %, low-speed 9/25 %, close-following 18/32 % of following time over 5,815 runs and 186,529 s), so H1 is largely refuted; what is missing is long continuous runs and a full queue cycle. Sample selection was corrected from longest-first to declared time-gap stratification. Phase P3: the previous '26/48 insertions rejected' statement was wrong - SUMO retries a blocked insertion on later steps; the old implementation stopped waiting after 0.25 s. Two verified native routes now load the observed state without distortion (leader tracking 0.013-0.112 m), and a control experiment shows the insertion-check-free route leaves the subsequent dynamics bit-identical. The weaker claim survives: observed congested following states often lie outside the frozen Krauss safety envelope, visible as a 0.05-0.70 s insertion delay. Phase P4 (324 independent SUMO runs, 12 pairs x 9 configurations x 3 shared seeds, 0 failures): raising tau is monotonically harmful (+18.3/+40.7/+72.5 pp paired, sign-consistent across all seeds), reducing minGap helps (-7.3 pp) while raising it hurts (+29.8), switching off the dawdling term helps (-6.3), and IDM at T=1.0 is the best configuration (-5.5 pp, 18/18 pairs) with its gain concentrated in the long-run window (-8.1 pp) rather than the local response (-0.09 pp). The independent Newell prototype lands at the same level (50.9 %) and degrades with tau in the same way, so the direction does not depend on model structure. Seed variability is 1.5-5.2 pp and grows with tau; the parameter effect is about 13.5x that noise. tau and minGap effects are strongly correlated across pairs (r = -0.94 and +0.82), so they are not separately identifiable on this sample, consistent with the practical-non-identifiability result of Wang et al. (2022). Phase P5 was gated shut because no configuration earned pair-level support, so no new macro contrast was run and RC1/RC2/RC3 are preserved. Gate stays pending_simulation_sample. 2026-10-21 AAD-0.5-CLOSURE: state support established at the aggregate level with the evidence-derived headway and a declared downstream supply (both calibration windows, five independent seeds, held-out domain transfer 0.851), but interaction compatibility is not established (local P2 rate 0.9-1.5 vs 17.0/23.5 per vehicle-hour); a discrete lane drop at matched declared capacity restores the P2 rate (18.2-25.5) but overshoots the mean state. Stage 0.5 not accepted.

results.name: Stage 0.5 real traffic formation reconstruction and conditional observed-geometry SUMO scene diagnostics
results.data_version_source: Two SHA-bound canonical calibration states 684a5f0b96dc4811... and 7b0ef830c97a981d...; bundled official NGSIM US-101 data-analysis reports; third window and locked holdout not read

core_metrics.jam_wave_origin: largest low-speed components first appear at y=500-650 m and expand upstream in both windows

results.current_conclusion: AAD-0.5-TR-RECON reconstructed the real traffic process and diagnosed the state mismatch. The observed local region sits just downstream of a Ventura Blvd on-ramp merge and just upstream of a Cahuenga Blvd off-ramp diverge, with a sixth auxiliary lane physically present inside the approved five-lane D1 region; both windows are on the congested branch (43.5/50.5 veh/km/lane at 10.51/7.92 m/s) while the same measured cross-section flow also exists on the free-flow branch. The largest low-speed waves first appear at the downstream end of the observation (y=500-650 m) and expand upstream, so the congested state is imported from an unobserved downstream supply. Three pre-declared SUMO diagnostics were executed: observed geometry plus observed boundary demand stays on the free-flow branch (23.90 m/s, 21.05 veh/km/lane, 1811 veh/h/lane); injecting the real observed congested state decays to free flow within 180 s; an admitted conditional 3-lane downstream supply reaches the congested branch but overshoots (6.76 m/s, 61.35 veh/km/lane, 1492 veh/h/lane). None reached the observed target envelope, so state support is Evidence Insufficient and the pre-declared stop rule was executed with no parameter search, no independent-seed repeat and no fourth construction. The congested-branch diagnosis shows the observed density and the observed net gap independently imply an effective Krauss time gap of about 1.53-1.63 s versus the frozen 1.0 s, which is the quantitative reason the same flow is reachable only on the free-flow branch; this is a Hypothesis requiring a controlled probe and a researcher decision.

results.name: Literature-grounded traffic-state definition sensitivity, spatial null model and leader-replay behaviour diagnostics
results.data_version_source: Two SHA-bound canonical calibration states 684a5f0b96dc4811... and 7b0ef830c97a981d...; third window and locked holdout not read
results.current_conclusion: AAD-0.5-LIT-CAL grounded every method in a full-text-verified source and tested the behaviour hypothesis at the individual-pair level. Phase A: the low-speed wave direction and origin are robust to ten state definitions (16/16 non-saturated rules grow upstream from y=500-650 m, backward speed 2.0-8.3 m/s), and the relative-speed definitions show spatial clustering beyond a per-time-step permutation null model in both windows; however the largest-component size under the absolute 10 m/s rule is NOT distinguishable from the null in 0750 (exceedance 0.999), so the earlier size claim is narrowed to the relative-speed definitions. Phase B replayed 24 leader-follower pairs (12 per window) through SUMO with TraCI-controlled leaders: leader tracking stayed within 0.013-0.112 m, but 26 of 48 pair-configuration initial states were rejected by SUMO's own Krauss insertion safety envelope (44%), which is itself a quantified behaviour-state mismatch concentrated in the congested window. tau=1.6 did not fix the following behaviour: paired Brockfeld gap error changed by +19.6 pp (95% CI [4.3, 35.5], 7 improved / 13 worsened) and the gap bias increased for 20/20 pairs (+5.6 m); NRMSE(speed) was essentially unchanged (+0.00). Stratified by observed time gap the candidate is much worse below 1.5 s (+56.7 and +63.8 pp) and neutral-to-slightly-better on speed in the 1.5-10 s stratum. The macro-derived 1.53-1.63 s is therefore narrowed to a congested-region equilibrium equivalent, not a usable single micro tau. Phase C was not executed under the pre-declared gate; RC1/RC2/RC3 are preserved unchanged. Gate stays pending_simulation_sample.

results.name: Literature-grounded method expansion: behavioural coverage, initialization fidelity, and bounded structure/parameter/randomness diagnostics
results.configuration_source: response_plan.json, init_plan.json, newell_plan.json (each SHA-bound before its batch); doc/literature-notes/stage_0_5_method_index.json
results.data_version_source: Two SHA-bound canonical calibration states 684a5f0b96dc4811... and 7b0ef830c97a981d...; third window and locked holdout not read
results.current_conclusion: AAD-0.5-METHOD-EXPANSION executed the literature-verified method expansion and diagnosed the real-to-SUMO mismatch across initialization, structure, parameters and randomness. Phase P2: all behavioural phases are present in the trajectories (stationary 40/52 %, accelerating 32/25 %, decelerating 28/24 %, low-speed 9/25 %, close-following 18/32 % of following time over 5,815 runs and 186,529 s), so H1 is largely refuted; what is missing is long continuous runs and a full queue cycle. Sample selection was corrected from longest-first to declared time-gap stratification. Phase P3: the previous '26/48 insertions rejected' statement was wrong - SUMO retries a blocked insertion on later steps; the old implementation stopped waiting after 0.25 s. Two verified native routes now load the observed state without distortion (leader tracking 0.013-0.112 m), and a control experiment shows the insertion-check-free route leaves the subsequent dynamics bit-identical. The weaker claim survives: observed congested following states often lie outside the frozen Krauss safety envelope, visible as a 0.05-0.70 s insertion delay. Phase P4 (324 independent SUMO runs, 12 pairs x 9 configurations x 3 shared seeds, 0 failures): raising tau is monotonically harmful (+18.3/+40.7/+72.5 pp paired, sign-consistent across all seeds), reducing minGap helps (-7.3 pp) while raising it hurts (+29.8), switching off the dawdling term helps (-6.3), and IDM at T=1.0 is the best configuration (-5.5 pp, 18/18 pairs) with its gain concentrated in the long-run window (-8.1 pp) rather than the local response (-0.09 pp). The independent Newell prototype lands at the same level (50.9 %) and degrades with tau in the same way, so the direction does not depend on model structure. Seed variability is 1.5-5.2 pp and grows with tau; the parameter effect is about 13.5x that noise. tau and minGap effects are strongly correlated across pairs (r = -0.94 and +0.82), so they are not separately identifiable on this sample, consistent with the practical-non-identifiability result of Wang et al. (2022). Phase P5 was gated shut because no configuration earned pair-level support, so no new macro contrast was run and RC1/RC2/RC3 are preserved. Gate stays pending_simulation_sample.

results.name: Conditional traffic-state support: real following relation, state domain, declared supply x behaviour grid, structural variant, frozen temporal validation
results.data_version_source: sealed Stage 0.2 canonical states of us101__0750_0805 (sha 684a5f0b…), us101__0805_0820 (sha 7b0ef830…), held-out us101__0820_0835 read only after freeze
results.current_conclusion: Conditional state support is established at the aggregate level (density, speed, flow, mean time headway) for both calibration windows with five independent seeds and it transfers to the held-out window, but interaction compatibility is NOT established: the state-matching configuration produces 0.9-1.5 local P2 events per vehicle-hour against 17.0/23.5 observed, with 35% less speed dispersion. At matched declared capacity a discrete lane drop restores the dispersion and the P2 rate (18.2-25.5) but overshoots the mean state. Supply level controls the mean state, supply form controls relative motion; no single declared encoding satisfies both. Stage 0.5 is therefore not accepted; the single remaining blocker is the interaction-compatibility layer.

results.name: Boundary arrival-timing audit, relative-speed wave diagnostic and paired uniform-vs-real arrival contrast
results.data_version_source: sealed Stage 0.2 canonical states of us101__0750_0805 and us101__0805_0820; the held-out us101__0820_0835 window was not read
results.current_conclusion: Restoring the real boundary arrival times does not close the interaction-compatibility gap. The mainline entry is queue-limited: declared mainline inter-arrival CV 0.25 vs 0.86 (0750) and 0.20 vs 0.91 (0805) collapses to realised 0.820 vs 0.831 and 0.788 vs 0.851, with mean insertion delays of 25-30 s and 4.5-5.6 s, so mainline arrival timing cannot be imposed at all. On-ramp arrival timing is imposed almost exactly (realised CV 1.397/1.412 vs 0.006/0.008). Under that de facto on-ramp-only contrast, speed dispersion moves toward the real value consistently (5/5 in both windows) but the closing-speed negative share worsens, the local P2 rate conflicts across windows, and no run reaches a corroborated upstream wave. Stage 0.5 therefore remains blocked by the interaction-compatibility layer, and boundary arrival structure is removed from the list of sufficient explanations. The corrected relative-speed wave diagnostic is validated and now discriminates real from simulated frames.
